concepts.rationale: Diva in Bucatarie documents toasted bread with garlic, olive oil and tomato topping. The definition preserves the named appetizer and does not label it traditional Romanian cuisine.
Laura Laurentiu lists bread, milk, egg, sugar and raisins and bakes the mixture. The definition preserves custard setting and does not equate soaking alone with the finished pudding.
Gina Bradea explicitly calls the filled, sauced oven-baked pancakes gratinate. The new term denotes an additional preparation rather than a renamed plain pancake.
Laura Laurentiu documents the potato-dough and cooked-dough plum dumplings separately, including boiling and sweet browned breadcrumbs. The definition avoids requiring potato in every variant.
The 2010 named-author banana recipe and Kitchen Affair ice-cream version establish two milk-based blended drink variants. The original definition covers either familiar preparation.
Adygio documents layered potatoes and minced meat baked together; Unilever separately documents the mashed-potato variant. The definition accommodates both ordinary forms.
The original e-Retete preparation uses boiled egg halves and a yolk/pate/mayonnaise filling. The definition describes the dish without asserting one compulsory filling.

Good Food distinguishes dried fine breadcrumbs and rolling-pin crushing; Laura Laurentiu uses them for breading meat. The definition distinguishes this prepared ingredient from arbitrary fresh crumbs.
e-Retete and Mega Image document pasta combined with vegetables as a salad, including grilled vegetables. The definition allows cooling and additional dressing or cheese.
Hutton explicitly adds separately boiled thin noodles to hot soup. The corrected definition allows this common serving method and avoids reshaping already cooked pasta.

items.rationale: The e-Retete method boils the eggs, removes the yolks and makes a creamy filling with mayonnaise before filling the whites. The pair captures recognizable essentials.
The same primary method explicitly includes pate in the yolk filling. The explanation retains mayonnaise and filling the boiled whites rather than implying uncooked eggs.
Adygio combines sliced potatoes and cooked minced pork filling in baked layers. The explanation states cooking, layering and the oven, making the two-input abstraction honest.
Unilever makes a minced-beef ragu and alternates it with mashed potato and vegetables before gratinating. This supports the alternate mash route.
Gina Bradea uses filled pancakes, cream and egg before baking. The explanation keeps the filling and oven step explicit; cream is not treated as sufficient without preparation.
The same primary recipe finishes assembled filled pancakes in the oven. This uses the existing cooked pancakes as an intermediate and identifies the additional sauce.
Laura Laurentiu makes plum dumplings using cooked-potato dough, then boils and coats them in sweet breadcrumbs. The potato/plum pairing is a familiar preparation, not raw mixing.
The separate original recipe uses cooked semolina dough, flour and eggs around plums, then boiling and breadcrumbs. The explanation names the suitable dough variant.
Kitchen Affair blends milk with vanilla ice cream and optional fruit. Ice cream is genuinely reused in a distinct drink; the recipe does not introduce a nutritional claim.
The replacement named-author 2010 recipe blends ripe banana and milk. Unsupported frozen-banana/spice wording was removed with the retired redirecting reference.
The primary Diva in Bucatarie recipe tops toasted garlic bread with chopped tomatoes and oil. The input already toasted bread is compatible with that sequence.
The same primary recipe toasts the bread before the tomato topping. This alternate plain-bread input explicitly includes toasting, preserving the named preparation.
The e-Retete original uses cooked pasta and vegetables, with oil and seasonings, as pasta salad. The explanation specifies the cooked/cooled preparation.
Mega Image publishes a pasta salad with grilled vegetables and parmesan. This supports a meaningful onward use of already grilled vegetables.
The original bread pudding combines milk, eggs and bread before baking. The explanation keeps egg, sweetening and setting explicit beyond the two selected inputs.
The same original includes raisins mixed through bread and a milk/egg custard before baking. The alternate pair preserves those necessary preparation steps.
Good Food explicitly supports crushing dried bread using a rolling pin. Drying and cooling are stated, so ordinary moist toast is not mistaken for ready dry crumbs.
Dry croutons are toasted bread pieces; crushing them finely follows the primary dry-breadcrumb method. The explanation accurately retains any original seasoning.
Laura Laurentiu documents thin meat covered with flour, egg and breadcrumbs before frying. The explanation includes the full breading sequence and keeps the existing Schnitzel result.
The cited original specifically uses chicken breast with flour, egg and breadcrumbs. The new prepared ingredient supplies a grounded alternative to the existing recipe.
The Hutton manufacturer recipe boils thin noodles separately before adding hot soup. The corrected explanation reuses already cooked pasta; it no longer stretches or cuts cooked pasta into a dough.
